name: Cable EZ-Bar Reverse Curl
summary: A cable isolation exercise that targets the brachialis and brachioradialis using a pronated grip on an EZ-bar attachment.

setup: Attach an EZ-bar to a low pulley cable station.
Stand facing the machine with feet hip-width apart and a slight bend in your knees.
Grasp the bar with a pronated (overhand) grip on the angled portions of the bar.
Stand fully upright with your arms extended downward, shoulders retracted, and elbows tucked close to your torso.
steps: Keeping your upper arms stationary against your sides, curl the bar upward by flexing your elbows.
Continue lifting until your forearms are nearly vertical and you achieve a strong contraction in the forearms and upper arms.
Pause briefly at the top while keeping your wrists rigid and neutral.
Lower the bar smoothly along the same path under control until your elbows are fully extended.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you curl the bar upward and inhale as you lower it back down.
cues: Keep elbows pinned to your ribs
Control the weight on the way down

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso to use momentum to move the weight.
common_faults.correction: Brace your core and keep your upper body still throughout the entire movement.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the elbows to drift forward or flare out.
common_faults.correction: Keep your upper arms stationary and tightly tucked to ensure the stress stays on the elbow flexors.

common_faults.fault: Letting the wrists extend back or flex excessively under load.
common_faults.correction: Keep your wrists firmly locked in a neutral alignment with your forearms.
